evals.prompt: The services nebula-demo-rca-frontend and nebula-demo-rca-backend have a history of repeated error alarms in this account. Regardless of whether they are erroring right now, analyze the architecture and tell me what structural problems are driving these recurring incidents. Do the work in this turn and give the full answer in your final message; do not hand it to a background task.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses the topology to see the front-end synchronously calls the single back-end, classifies the back-end as a single point of failure, names the synchronous coupling and the cascade-failure path, and returns an architectural-debt verdict rather than two separate per-incident findings.
assertions: The output presents separate findings, each labelled with one of the catalog's names: single point of failure, synchronous coupling with no fallback, and cascade-failure path
Each finding is given a severity of High, Medium or Low, and the findings are ordered by severity
Each finding states the resource path (for example frontend -> backend), the evidence behind it, why it matters, and a proposed remediation
The output ties the two error alarms to one structural cause and says whether Topology or Proactive Incident Prevention output was available as an input
The output proposes remediation without executing any change and says it made no changes

evals.prompt: I already use DevOps Agent's Topology and Proactive Incident Prevention. Does the RCA architectural anti-pattern catalog skill just repeat what they tell me?
evals.expected_output: The agent explains it consumes the Topology graph and Proactive Incident Prevention output rather than re-running them, and that its distinct contribution is classifying findings against a named anti-pattern catalog and reporting architectural debt in that vocabulary.
assertions: The output states it consumes Topology and Proactive Incident Prevention rather than re-implementing them
The output identifies the named anti-pattern catalog as its distinct contribution
The output states the skill adds a named anti-pattern classification layer on top of existing cross-incident analysis, and does not say DevOps Agent lacks that analysis

assertions: The output states the plan is proposed for human approval and that nothing has been changed
